The London Itinerary

26 · 27 · 28 · 29 October 2026

Mon 26

Landing, then Camden

Half the day is travel. One neighbourhood in the evening, nothing else.

  1. 09:3010:35

    Flight FR8317

    Malpensa to Stansted, 1h05

    Where
    Milano Malpensa, terminal on your boarding pass
    Be there
    07:30, two hours before
    Cost
    Paid, reference in your email
    Ticket
    In the Ryanair app. Printed passes are refused at the gate
    Feels like
    Airport noise, queues, announcements. Ear defenders or headphones in your hand luggage.
    What you do here
    • Check in on the app before you leave home.
    • Both passports in hand luggage, not in the case.
    • Lands 10:35 London time, which is one hour behind Italy.
    Check in
  2. 11:3012:20

    Stansted airport to Liverpool Street

    Journey

    From
    Stansted Airport station, under the terminal, follow the signs
    To
    London Liverpool Street
    How
    Stansted Express, a normal train. Every 15 minutes
    How long
    48 minutes
    Pay
    Buy online before the trip, from £9.90 each. Contactless works too, but costs about £21.90 on the day. Oyster is not accepted
    Step by step
    1. Come out of arrivals and follow the signs down to the station.
    2. Show the ticket on your phone at the barrier.
    3. Any train on the platform goes to Liverpool Street. Sit anywhere.
    4. Stay on until the last stop.
    Buy ticketsRoute
  3. 12:4014:00

    Leadenhall Market, and lunch

    The Diagon Alley of the first film, and the first food since Italy

    Open
    Passage always open, food counters from 11:00
    Cost
    £6 to £14 each depending where you eat
    How long
    1 hour 20
    Address
    Gracechurch Street, EC3V 1LT, 10 minutes on foot from Liverpool Street
    Feels like
    Covered market, echoey, busy at lunchtime with office workers. Tables out on the cobbles.
    What you do here
    • Victorian covered market of 1881, painted ironwork and a glass roof. This is where Hagrid and Harry walk to the Leaky Cauldron in the first film.
    • The blue optician's door at 4 Bull's Head Passage is the Leaky Cauldron entrance. It is a working coffee house now, Two Eyes, if you want a coffee in it.
    • Three doors along the same passage is House of Wonders, a Harry Potter shop that opened in October 2025. Wands, robes, jewellery, clothing and homeware, plus Fantastic Beasts and Game of Thrones. Free to walk in. They publish no opening hours anywhere, and Leadenhall shops usually run about 10:00 to 18:00 on weekdays, so it should be open when you are there at lunchtime.
    • Where to eat, cheapest first. Oriani, an Italian cafe with outdoor tables on the cobbles: a small pasta is about £5.55 and fresh orange juice £3. Baba Ganoush, Lebanese, shawarma and big platters, one reviewer calls the platter great value. Tortilla, rated 4.7 from 2,065, big burritos, cheapest price band. Banh Mi Aha, Vietnamese, banh mi and pho.
    • Boom Bap Burger is rated 4.8 but a reviewer worked out £23.10 a head with the service charge and thought it steep.
    • Skip the Lamb Tavern unless you want the room. Fish and chips there is £21 and the pie £29.50.
    • None of it is British food. The British option in the market is the expensive pub.
    • If nothing appeals, do not force it. Walk the market, get the train home, and eat at Marina Cafe on the High Road, 8 minutes from the flat, £8 to £12 each.
    PhotosWalk there
  4. 14:0014:45

    Tower of London and Tower Bridge, from outside

    Ten minutes on foot, and you pay nothing

    Open
    The streets, always
    Cost
    Free. Going inside is about £35 each and takes 3 hours, so you are not doing that
    How long
    45 minutes
    Address
    10 minutes on foot south from Leadenhall
    Feels like
    Open riverside walk. Wind off the water. You keep moving, you do not queue.
    What you do here
    • Walk down Gracechurch Street to the river. The Tower appears on your left, the whole castle, the walls and the moat, and you see all of it from the public path without a ticket.
    • Keep going and Tower Bridge is right there. You can walk out onto it. The view back at the Tower from the middle of the bridge is the postcard one.
    • This is your only look at the Thames on this trip, so take the minute to stand and look at it.
    • You have backpacks on, but they are backpacks, not cases, so this is fine.
    • Finish at Tower Hill station, which is 3 minutes from the bridge.
    WalkPhotos

  8. 17:1520:15

    Camden Town

    A neighbourhood, not a shop. Four hours, all on foot

    Photos from Wikimedia, CC licensed

    Open
    Markets to 19:00, Hawley Wharf to 20:00, bars to 23:00
    Cost
    Free to walk around
    How long
    16:30 to about 20:45
    Address
    Camden High Street to Camden Lock, NW1
    Feels like
    The loudest place on the trip, and the best. Crowds, music from shops, food smells, uneven ground. Leave when you have had enough, not when you have seen everything.
    What you do here
    • Everything below is within a ten minute walk of everything else.
    • The area runs from Camden Town station north along the high street to the canal at Camden Lock.
    • Loud, crowded, covered in graffiti and painted shopfronts. That is the point of it.
    • Camden is where punk, goth and Britpop all actually happened, which is why it is on this trip and not in a drawer.
    Map

  13. 20:4521:30

    Fish and chips at Big Bite

    Proper chippy, five minutes from the flat

    Open
    Monday 12:00 to 22:00
    Cost
    About £29 for the two of you
    How long
    45 minutes
    Address
    39 Walm Lane, NW2 4QU
    Feels like
    Small chippy with tables, warm, quick. Quiet at that hour on a Monday.
    What you do here
    • Rated 4.5 from 590 people, and the best rated chippy near the flat.
    • Prices from their menu: cod, haddock, plaice or rock all £12.00. Chips £3.50 a portion or £2.50 a half portion. Mushy peas £1.10, homemade tartare £0.80, pickled gherkin £0.50.
    • If you do not want a whole fish: the special is cod bites with chips for £8.70, which is the right size for two people who do not eat much.
    • Pies are £3.00, steak and kidney, chicken and mushroom, beef and onion. Proper chippy food, no kebab and no curry on the menu.
    • One reviewer calls it the best chippy in Willesden Green. Another says the fish is crispy outside and tender inside and the chips are always fresh.
    • They serve wine too, and the room has tables so you can sit.
    MenuWalk there
Tue 27

The full day

Baker Street in the morning, Westminster and Soho in the afternoon, a film near home at night.

  1. 08:1509:00

    Breakfast at Arthur's Cafe

    Best rated cafe in the neighbourhood, and the cheapest

    Open
    From 06:00
    Cost
    £6 to £9 each
    How long
    45 minutes
    Address
    Station Terrace, Kensal Rise, NW10 5RX, 12 minutes on foot
    Feels like
    Small family cafe, checked tablecloths, warm and busy. Quiet before eight.
    What you do here
    • Rated 4.7 from 576 people. Red checked tablecloths, mugs of tea, cooked to order.
    • Breakfast is served all day and you build it. Egg with two bacon and sausage £5.95. Two eggs, two bacon and toast £5.95. Egg, two bacon and chips £6.95. Porridge with honey and banana £4.95.
    • Breakfast number 1 is the full version: 2 eggs, 2 bacon, sausage, beans, 2 toast and a mug of tea, £8.95.
    • Extras £1.50 each if you want to add something. Mug of tea £1.60, cappuccino £2.95, fresh orange juice £3.95.
    • Cheaper than anywhere else near the flat, and by a long way better reviewed.

  3. 09:3010:15

    Sherlock Holmes Museum

    Victorian house done as 221b Baker Street

    Photos from Wikimedia, CC licensed

    Open
    09:30 to 18:00 daily, last entry 17:30
    Cost
    £19 each, book online
    How long
    45 minutes
    Address
    221b Baker Street, NW1 6XE
    Feels like
    Small rooms, narrow stairs, people close together. Forty five minutes and you are out.
    What you do here
    • Book the timed ticket before the trip. The queue outside has no shelter.
    • The first floor study is the main room: deerstalker, violin, pipe, magnifying glass.
    • Watson's room and Mrs Hudson's floor are above it.
    • The top floor stages scenes from the cases with wax figures.
    • A Victorian policeman stands at the door and will pose with you.
    • Four floors of narrow stairs and no lift.
    Book tickets

  5. 10:5011:45

    Changing the Guard at Horse Guards

    The mounted one, and it happens every single day

    Time
    11:00, every day. 10:00 on Sundays
    Cost
    Free
    How long
    About 45 minutes
    Address
    Horse Guards Parade, Whitehall, SW1A 2AX
    Feels like
    Outdoors, cobbled parade ground, horses. Crowded but nothing like Buckingham Palace.
    What you do here
    • This is the Household Cavalry, so there are horses. The one at Buckingham Palace runs Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Sunday. There is no Sunday on this trip, Monday is your arrival day and Wednesday is the studio, so this is the one that works.
    • Get there by 10:50 for a decent spot. It is much less crowded than Buckingham Palace.
    • There is a second ceremony at 16:00 daily if you ever miss the morning one.
    • Horse Guards is on Whitehall, a 5 minute walk from Westminster station.

  6. 11:4512:30

    Big Ben, Westminster and the river

    Close up this time, not in passing

    Open
    Streets and bridge, always
    Cost
    Free
    How long
    45 minutes
    Address
    Parliament Square and Westminster Bridge, SW1A
    Feels like
    Wide open, windy on the bridge, traffic behind you. Best light of the day.
    What you do here
    • Walk 5 minutes down Whitehall from Horse Guards and the tower is in front of you. Stand under it. It is much bigger up close than photographs suggest.
    • Westminster Bridge is right there. Walk out onto it for the view back at Parliament and along the Thames.
    • Westminster station itself is the one from the fifth film, where Mr Weasley cannot work the ticket barrier.
    • Then walk back up Whitehall to Trafalgar Square, about 10 minutes, and Covent Garden is 8 minutes beyond that.

    Lunch at Mother Mash

    Pie, mash and gravy, which is the actual English dish

    Photos from Wikimedia, CC licensed

  10. 15:3017:15

    National Gallery

    National art collection, free, on Trafalgar Square

    Photos from Wikimedia, CC licensed

    Open
    10:00 to 18:00
    Cost
    Free, reserve a timed ticket
    How long
    2 hours
    Address
    Trafalgar Square, WC2N 5DN
    Feels like
    Busy at the entrance, much quieter in the side rooms. Benches everywhere. Half term week means school groups until about 15:30.
    What you do here
    • Reserve the free ticket online first. It is UK school half term and it will be busy.
    • Pick up the room map at the door, or use the room finder on their site, because paintings move.
    • Van Gogh, Sunflowers.
    • Turner, The Fighting Temeraire.
    • Van Eyck, The Arnolfini Portrait, and look at the mirror on the back wall.

    • Leave by 16:20. The pub is five minutes away and the bookshops shut at 19:00.

  11. 17:2518:15

    Charing Cross Road bookshops

    Second hand and rare books, the cheap kind and the dear kind

    Photos from Wikimedia, CC licensed

    Open
    Until 19:00 and 19:15
    Cost
    Free to browse. Books from a couple of pounds
    How long
    50 minutes
    Address
    56 and 72 Charing Cross Road, WC2H, 3 minutes from the pub
    What you do here
    • Any Amount of Books at number 56 is the one you asked for. A reviewer calls it the best second hand bookshop in London, consistently interesting and low priced.
    • Go behind the counter, there is another room of books back there. There is a clearance area downstairs as well.
    • Stock goes back to the early 1800s, so this is where you find something genuinely old without auction prices.
    • Henry Pordes at number 72, a hundred metres up, holds the rare and first editions. Prices there are high and some shelves say do not touch. Good to look at.
    • Cecil Court, the Victorian alley of antiquarian dealers, is one minute away if you want to walk down it. Prettier, dearer, smaller.
    Walk there
  12. 18:2018:35

    Goodwin's Court

    Twenty metres of gas lamps, and it costs nothing

    Open
    Always, it is a public alley
    Cost
    Free
    How long
    15 minutes
    Address
    Between St Martin's Lane and Bedfordbury, WC2N 4LL
    Feels like
    Narrow, dark, silent. Nobody there. Two minutes off a busy street.
    What you do here
    • A row of 18th century houses with bulging curved glass shop windows and gas lamps that still work. The frontages are black.
    • There are no shops and no signs. You walk in, you look, you walk out.
    • It is widely named as the visual inspiration for Diagon Alley and Knockturn Alley. Nothing was filmed here, and guides say so plainly, but you understand where the idea came from as soon as you are inside.
    • Entrance is easy to miss. From St Martin's Lane look for a narrow gap with steps.
    • From here it is 5 minutes north to the market.
    Map

    Dinner at Seven Dials Market

    A covered market of counters, you each pick your own

    Open
    Tuesday 12:00 to 22:00
    Cost
    Street food prices, roughly £10 to £15 a plate
    How long
    1 hour 30
    Address
    Earlham Street, WC2H 9LX, 8 minutes from the bookshops
    Feels like
    Busy covered market, echoey, warm inside. Outside tables are calmer.
    What you do here
    • Rated 4.5 from 9,398 people. Two floors of separate kitchens with loose tables in the middle, so you each order what you want and nothing repeats.

    • After: Covent Garden station is 5 minutes, Leicester Square 4.

    Cinema, optional

    Only if you still want to be out

    Open
    Until midnight
    Cost

    Feels like
    Vue is an ordinary big cinema, bright and easy. The Lexi is small and quiet.
    What you do here
    • Vue Finchley Road is the one for a new release. It is an ordinary modern multiplex in a shopping centre, nothing charming, it just shows everything that is out.

Your birthday

One coach you cannot miss, then the whole day at the studio.

    Where the studio coach picks you up

    Cost
    Paid, reference in your email

    Busy pavement outside a main station. Get there at 09:15 so you are not rushing.

    Say it is your birthday, twice

    Before you go in, not after

    Cost
    Free
    Where
    At the ticket desk, and again at the Great Hall doors
    How long
    An hour, because entry is 11:30
    Why
    You cannot get this once you are inside
    Feels like
    Thirty seconds of talking to staff. Worth more than anything you could buy in there.
    What you do here
    • The coach gets in about 10:30 and the entry time on your ticket is 11:30, so you have an hour in the lobby first. Bag drop, the Digital Guide desk and the toilets are all out here.
    • Tell the person at the ticket desk that it is your birthday. Visitors report being given a Star for the Day badge there, and a second, different badge from another steward.
    • Then say it again to whoever is on the doors of the Great Hall. One visitor writes that telling staff it is your birthday gets you the chance to open the Great Hall doors yourself. That is the opening moment of the tour, with the whole group standing behind you.
    • Do it before you go through, not later. Nobody can hand it to you once you are inside.
    • Pick up the free Activity Passport at the same time. Golden Snitch hunt, puzzles, and stamps you collect at Platform 9 and at Gringotts. If the Dark Mark trail is running this year, that is two stamp trails in one day.
    • There is a Happee Birthdae Harry cake, chocolate fudge with pink and green frosting, but it serves 6 to 10 people and has to be ordered by phone at least 72 hours ahead. Too big for two.
    • Take the power bank. You will photograph everything, and inside they only sell chargers in the shop.

    Warner Bros. Studio Tour

    The real Harry Potter film sets at Leavesden

    Photos from Wikimedia, CC licensed

    Open
    Your booking blocks 7 hours
    Cost
    Paid, £250 for the two of you

    Three and a half hours is normal

    Feels like
    Large indoor sets, controlled lighting, some loud sound effects and a wind machine in the Forbidden Forest. Self paced, with benches and a big café halfway.
    What you do here
    • The Great Hall is the opening room, and it is timed, so you start there.
    • Board the Hogwarts Express carriage on the Platform 9¾ set.
    • Photograph Diagon Alley from the far end looking back down the street.
    • Dumbledore's office and the Forbidden Forest.
    • The model of Hogwarts, lit through a full day and night cycle, comes near the end.
    • The last room is Ollivanders: a wall of wand boxes with the name of every cast and crew member on them. It opens straight into the shop.
    • Butterbeer is at the Butterbeer Bar and again at the Backlot Cafe, halfway through, outside by the Knight Bus. The studio is the only place in Europe you can drink it on tap.
    • On allergies the two sources disagree. The studio’s own FAQ says Butterbeer is suitable for gluten, wheat and nut allergies. Your Golden Tours ticket says it may contain nuts. If it matters to either of you, ask at the counter on the day rather than trusting either line.
    • Have the Butterbeer at the Backlot, but do not eat there. That cafe is where the bad reviews are: cold chips, poor meat, and one couple paid £40 for two Butterbeers, a hot dog and a burger.
    • It is your birthday. Buy the stupid souvenir.

  11. 19:3021:30

    Birthday dinner, pick on the day

    The only card with options, choose when you know how the shopping went

    When
    19:30, after Soho
    How long
    About 2 hours
    Getting there
    All of them are 5 to 20 minutes by tube from King's Cross
    Note
    Nothing here is licensed Harry Potter. Licensed does not exist in London.
    Feels like
    Three very different rooms. Decide on the night.
    What you do here
    • CITTIE OF YORKE, 22 High Holborn. Rated 4.5 from 3,271. A hall first built in the 15th century, rebuilt in the 1920s, with a vaulted ceiling and enclosed wooden cubicles you sit inside on your own. The closest thing London has to a Three Broomsticks. Sausage and mash with onion gravy £15.95, chickpea and sweet potato curry £15.95, scampi £17.00, steak and ale pie with mash £18.50, fish and chips £19.25. Sticky toffee £7.75. Samuel Smith beers, much cheaper than the rest of London. Closed Sunday. Piccadilly line from King's Cross to Holborn, 5 minutes.
    • BRASSERIE ZEDEL, 20 Sherwood Street, Piccadilly. A 1930s Paris art deco hall, marble columns and gold, underground. Nothing wizarding about it, but it is the cheapest good dinner in central London: two courses £16.95, three courses £19.95. The Wednesday plat du jour is smoked haddock florentine at £21.50. There is also a Formule at £28.95 with three courses plus a drink. Their menu says they can do two courses in 45 minutes if you tell the server.
    • THE LAST JUDGMENT, 95 Chancery Lane. The Union Bank of London building of 1865, listed, with gold gilded ceilings, chandeliers and a mezzanine dining room looking down on the hall. Grand and bank-like, which is why people compare it to Gringotts, though nothing was filmed here. Fish and chips £22, Guinness £7.75. Five minutes on foot from the Cittie of Yorke.
    • Add your own here. This card is the one to edit.

Off the edge

Two places do not fit on a London map. The studio at Leavesden is 30km north west of King’s Cross, about an hour by the coach. Stansted is 50km north east, 48 minutes from Liverpool Street.

  • How London transport works

    Read this once, it covers every journey in this file

    Cost
    Never more than £8.90 each per day on tubes and trains
    Buses
    £1.75 flat, tap only when you get on
    Cards
    One bank card or phone each, used all day, every time
    Exception
    Contactless works on the Stansted Express, but book online for £9.90 instead of £21.90
    What you do here
    • The tube lines have names and colours. Jubilee is silver grey, Elizabeth is purple, Circle is yellow. A line is just a train.
    • You do not buy tickets. You tap your bank card or your phone on the yellow reader at the gate going in, and again coming out.
    • Tap out every time, or you get charged the maximum fare.
    • Use the same card or phone all day. If you tap in with the phone and out with the card, it counts as two people and the daily cap breaks.
    • You each need your own card or phone. You cannot share.
    • Platforms are signed by direction, for example Jubilee towards Stanmore is northbound. Check the direction, not just the line.
    Journey planner

    • In the app: photo of the passport, hold the passport to the back of the phone to read the chip, scan his face, a selfie, a few questions, pay.
    • The official app is called just UK ETA and the publisher shows as Home Office. Anything called UK ETA Visa Services or similar is a private company charging more.
    • The official deadline is three working days, so if a photo or the chip fails he wants to find out now.

Worth knowing

It gets dark at about 16:45. The clocks go back on 25 October, the day before you land, so the afternoons end early.

It is UK school half term, so museums, the studio tour and central London are busier than normal.

Willesden Green station has stairs only, no lift, in both directions.

Bring an umbrella. Late October in London is not a maybe.

Keep your phone in your pocket near roads. Phone snatching from bikes happens on busy shopping streets.

Documents

The passports, the tickets and the booking references are not on this page. They are on a separate one, behind a passphrase.

Open the private page

Flight itinerary, studio tour ticket, coach voucher, the ETA and the passport. Once it has loaded it works with no signal, same as this page.

Open the private page

It asks for the passphrase. Tick the box to be remembered so your phone only asks once.

Why it is separate

This page is public. Anyone with the link opens it, which is the point, it is just an itinerary.

The other one is encrypted, not hidden. Without the passphrase there is nothing readable in it, not even in the source.

Packing

One backpack, four days

Wear the heavy things, pack the light ones. Weather is 12 to 14 by day and it gets dark at 16:45.

Kept after you fly. Nothing here is deleted, it just stops being the thing you open first.

  • Wear it, do not pack it

    The trick for fitting four days in one backpack

    Why
    Anything on your body is not in the bag
    What
    Your heaviest layer
    Weather
    12 to 14 by day, 7 to 9 at night, light rain likely
    Dark
    Sunset about 16:45, the clocks go back on 25 October
    What you do here
    • Fly wearing the waterproof jacket, the heaviest leggings or trousers, and the bulkier trainers.
    • London wind means a hooded waterproof beats an umbrella. Take a small folding umbrella anyway, because some of the rain comes with no wind at all.
    • You are outside most of each day, so layers you can add and remove work better than one thick coat.

  • In the backpack

    Four days, three nights, one wash if you need it

    Nights
    3
    Days out
    4
    Laundry
    The flat is yours for three nights, so one wash is possible
    Rule
    One spare of everything, not two
    What you do here
    • Two more leggings besides the pair you travel in.
    • Four t-shirts. One a day plus one spare. Long sleeve is more useful than short at this temperature.
    • One t-shirt to sleep in, or reuse one from the day.
    • One jumper or hoodie. Just one. It goes under the jacket on the colder days.
    • Underwear for four days. Socks for five, because socks are the thing that gets wet.
    • A second pair of shoes, the lighter ones. Swapping to a dry pair rescues a rainy day.
    • A thin scarf. It takes no space and does more than a thick coat.
    • A hat if you feel the cold on your head.

  • In the shoulder bag

    The things you need without taking the backpack off

    Charging
    A power bank is close to essential
    Why
    You use the phone all day for maps and this file
    Money
    Contactless card for every tap
    Papers
    See the Papers tab
    What you do here
    • Passport, boarding passes, the ETA reference, and the booking numbers.
    • Power bank and cable. You will be on the phone all day for the map and the itinerary.
    • The card you tap on the Underground. Same card in and out, every time.
    • A little cash for the places that only take it.
    • The folding umbrella lives here, not in the backpack.

  • What not to bring

    Things that eat space for nothing

    Cabin bag
    Ryanair small bag rules, so keep it to the one backpack
    Space
    Every item you skip is one you can buy
    Note
    There are shops everywhere
    Weight
    You carry this on Monday until 15:00
    What you do here
    • No second jumper. No third pair of shoes.
    • No full bottles of anything. Buy shampoo there if you need it, or use what the flat has.
    • Do not pack a heavy coat as well as the waterproof. Pick one.
    • On Monday you carry all of this until check in at 15:00, including the walk around Leadenhall and the Tower. Pack for that, not for the flat.

How to spend less

Eat at markets and food halls. Camden and BOXPARK are £10 to £15 against £25 for a sit down meal.

The free things are the good things. The National Gallery, Leadenhall Market, Covent Garden and every bookshop on the list cost nothing to walk into.

Book the trains now. £9.90 in advance against about £21.90 on the day, four times over.

One card each, tapped in and out all day, so the daily cap actually applies.

    Busy pub downstairs, the recreated sitting room is quiet upstairs.

01Birthday freebies you can actually get

Every name below links straight to its sign-up page. Web means you can do it in a browser from anywhere. App only means it exists solely inside the UK app, which needs a UK app store account. Easy to switch on Android, more of a fight on iPhone.

Start with the six web ones. They take about fifteen minutes together.

04Free museums, and which days they open

Wikimedia Commons, credits below

Monday 26 is the awkward day

Sir John Soane’s, the Grant Museum, the Petrie and the Hunterian are all shut on Mondays. Soane’s is shut Tuesday too, so Wednesday or Thursday are your only shots at it.

Monday works for the City instead, which is where you already are. The Bank of England Museum, Guildhall and the roof gardens are all open, and all within ten minutes of Leadenhall.

The small ones, which are the good ones

OpenWhereNote
Wed and ThuSir John Soane’s Museum, 13 Lincoln’s Inn FieldsAn architect’s house left exactly as he died in it, packed floor to ceiling. Wed to Sun 10:00 to 17:00. Free, walk in, no booking
Any dayThe Wallace Collection, Manchester SquareArmour downstairs, Rembrandt upstairs. Daily 10:00 to 17:00. Already in your Spares
Mon to FriBank of England Museum, Bartholomew Lane10:00 to 17:00, closed weekends. You can lift a real gold bar. Free, no booking
Tue to ThuGrant Museum of Zoology, UCL, Gower StreetSkeletons and specimen jars in one Victorian room. 13:00 to 17:00 only. Free
Tue to ThuPetrie Museum, UCL, Malet PlaceEgyptian archaeology, 80,000 objects, almost nobody there. 13:00 to 17:00. Free
Tue to ThuHunterian Museum, Lincoln’s Inn FieldsSurgical specimens, not for everyone. 10:00 to 17:00. Free, book ahead to skip the queue
Any dayGuildhall Art Gallery, Guildhall YardFree, and London’s Roman amphitheatre is in the basement

Mon to FriThe Library at Willesden Green, 95 High Road NW10Award winning building, free, with Brent Museum on the second floor, a café and a bookshop. Open to 20:00. Five minutes from the flat
Wed and ThuKensal Rise Library, Bathurst Gardens NW10Community run by volunteers who saved it from closing. Wed 14:00 to 19:00, Thu and Fri 14:00 to 17:00. Closed Mon and Tue, so Wednesday or Thursday only. Free, donations welcome
DaylightKensal Green Cemetery, Harrow Road W10A Victorian garden cemetery with Gothic monuments and catacombs. Brunel and Thackeray are buried here. Free to walk, self guided routes online. About as far from a tourist trap as London gets
Two windowsNeasden Temple, Pramukh Swami Road NW10Free entry. Hand carved Italian marble and Bulgarian limestone with no nails or steel in the structure. Open 09:00 to 12:15 and 16:00 to 18:00. Modest dress, shoes off. 20 minutes by bus and almost entirely missed by visitors
VariesSt Mary’s Willesden, Neasden Lane NW10A 12th century parish church with a Black Madonna and a medieval font, marooned in suburban Brent. Free, but opening depends on volunteers
DailyQueen’s Park, Roundwood Park, Gladstone ParkAll free. Already in Your street. Gladstone Park has the view south across London
08Free to browse. Books, comics, records

Cecil Court, the whole street

SinceWhereNote
1893Watkins Books, 19 to 21 Cecil CourtLondon’s oldest occult and esoteric bookshop. They do not mind browsers
RareMarchpane, 16 Cecil CourtRare children’s books and illustration, famous for its Alice in Wonderland holdings
SignedGoldsboro Books, Cecil CourtSigned first editions, a real collectors’ destination

Other bookshops worth the walk

WhereWhatNote
King’s CrossWord on the Water, Regent’s Canal towpathA 1920s Dutch barge full of secondhand books with a wood stove burning and occasional jazz on the roof. Hours go on their Facebook rather than a website, so check the day before. The natural end of the canal walk
Museum StThe Atlantis Bookshop, 49a Museum StreetOccult bookshop opened in 1922, a few doors from the British Museum. Tiny and atmospheric
King’s CrossHousmans, 5 Caledonian RoadRadical bookshop running since 1945
Marchmont StJudd Books, 82 Marchmont StreetSecondhand and remaindered, cheap and good. Two minutes from Skoob
BloomsburyLondon Review Bookshop, 14 Bury PlaceBehind the British Museum. The best curated general bookshop in London, with a cake shop attached

Comics and manga

WhereWhatNote
SohoGosh! Comics, 1 Berwick StreetOpen 10:30 to 19:00 seven days. Widely rated the best in London and the least intimidating to browse. Already in your Spares
Covent GdnOrbital Comics, 8 Great Newport StreetHas a free comic art gallery at the back, and it is thirty seconds from the Death Eater alley

Records

WhereWhatNote
PortobelloHonest Jon’s, 278 Portobello RoadTrading since 1974. Reggae, jazz, world. Open midweek unlike the antique market, so this is how you get something out of a Portobello trip on your days
SohoReckless Records and Sister Ray, Berwick StreetBoth on the same street as Gosh!, so one stop covers three shops
09Free events in your four days
WhenWhatNote
Every dayThe 16:00 dismount parade, Horse GuardsRuns daily in the courtyard, much smaller than the morning ceremony, and you can stand a few feet away. Free, no ticket. The backup if you ever miss the 11:00

Half term programmes at the free museums usually publish two to four weeks ahead, so a look at londonist.com in mid October will turn up more free events than exist online today.

10Dates to act on, in order
DateWhatWhy
NowCosta Club, Greggs, Caffè Nero, Krispy Kreme, Turtle BayNo deadline, but do them together in one sitting and forget about it
NowScience Museum free ticketRequired, not optional, and it is half term
30 SeptBill’sFour week lead time for the prosecco or pancakes
1 OctCeremony of the Keys, if you want itCorrection to what people will tell you. It is no longer free and the ballot is gone. Historic Royal Palaces sells tickets from £10, released 13:00 on the first working day of the month for the following month, and it sells out in minutes
Mon 5 OctSky Garden free ticketsReleased Monday mornings for three weeks ahead
Mon 13 OctHorizon 22 free tickets, 10:00Released 10:00 every Monday for 14 days ahead. This is the exact Monday for your dates
14 OctODEON Extras, GAIL’s, Zizzi, PrezzoTwo week lead times. Last safe date
Early OctCheck changing-guard.comThe October 2026 schedule was not published yet. The Mon, Wed, Fri and Sun pattern is the usual one but it is not confirmed
11All of it, grouped by area

Everything here sits somewhere you already pass through. If an hour opens up, look at the area you are standing in.

AreaFree therePick one
The CityLeadenhall Market, the Leaky Cauldron door, The Garden at 120, Horizon 22, Sky Garden, One New Change roof, Bank of England Museum, Guildhall Art Gallery, St Dunstan in the East, Postman’s Park, Old Bailey galleryThe Garden at 120, three minutes from Leadenhall and nobody knows about it. Monday, before you head north
King’s CrossPlatform 9¾, St Pancras, British Library Treasures Gallery, Word on the Water, Housmans, Judd Books, SkoobThe Treasures Gallery, open to 20:00. Wednesday, while you wait for dinner
Covent GardenGoodwin’s Court, Cecil Court, Seven Dials, Neal’s Yard, Leicester Square statue trail, Orbital Comics, the Great Newport Street alley, National Gallery, National Portrait GalleryCecil Court, which is your whole trip in one street. Tuesday, it is already next door to the bookshops
SohoHouse of MinaLima, Gosh! Comics, Reckless Records, Sister RayGosh! Comics, on the same street as the two record shops. Wednesday, right after MinaLima
HolbornSir John Soane’s Museum, Hunterian MuseumSoane’s, five minutes from the Cittie of Yorke. Wednesday, if you get back early enough
BloomsburyBritish Museum, Grant Museum, Petrie Museum, Atlantis Bookshop, London Review BookshopThe Petrie, 80,000 objects and nobody in it. On the way between King’s Cross and Soho
WestminsterHorse Guards, the 16:00 dismount, Scotland Place, Great Scotland Yard, Lambeth BridgeThe 16:00 dismount, if you ever miss the 11:00
MaryleboneThe Wallace CollectionTen minutes from Baker Street. Tuesday, if the Sherlock museum runs short
CamdenCamden Market, Regent’s Canal towpath, Primrose HillThe canal walk from Little Venice, which starts near you
Your streetThe Library at Willesden Green, Kensal Rise Library, Kensal Green Cemetery, Neasden Temple, St Mary’s Willesden, Honest Jon’s on Portobello, three parks, Hampstead HeathNeasden Temple, and it is practically local to you
